title: Fish and Poultry Processing
shortDescription: Fish freshness, handling and preservation; poultry slaughter-line steps and quality.
genZNote: Fish goes off in hours, chicken in days — both need an obsessive cold chain. TMA = fishy smell, remember the villain.

sections.heading: Fish Processing
bullets: Composition: water 65–80%, protein 15–20%, oils rich in EPA/DHA.
Handling: bleed/gut, wash, ice (0 °C) quickly; rigor then autolysis then bacterial spoilage.
Freshness indices: eye, gills, texture, odour, TVB-N, TMA, K-value, histamine for scombroid species.

Processing: chilling, freezing (−18 °C or below; individually quick frozen), canning (tuna, sardine), drying and salting (Bombay duck), smoking, surimi, fish sauce, fish meal and oil, chitin from crustacean shells.
Safety: Vibrio, Listeria, histamine, parasites (Anisakis), heavy metals.

steps.name: Bleeding and scalding
steps.explanation: Scald ~50–60 °C depending on soft or hard scald.

steps.name: Defeathering and evisceration
steps.explanation: Mechanical pickers; removal of viscera with inspection.

steps.name: Grading, cutting, packing
steps.explanation: Weight and quality grading; MAP or vacuum.

sections.heading: Quality and Safety
bullets: Poultry carries Salmonella and Campylobacter: avoid cross-contamination; cook to core 74 °C.
Broilers reach slaughter weight at ~5–7 weeks; layers are for eggs.
Value-added products: sausages, nuggets, marinated cuts; additives and cures regulated by FSSAI.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Fish and poultry are highly perishable and require rapid chilling, hygienic dressing and controlled processing to preserve quality and safety.
keyFacts: Fish: ice at 0 °C; TMA and TVB-N indices.

commonTraps: Do not rinse raw poultry as a safety measure.
